prerequisites: fundamentals of geometry and mathematics at the secondary school level

learning_outcomes.text: Introduce students to the principles of representation and important properties of some curves and surfaces.
Introduce students to the basics of the international language of engineers, i.e. descriptive geometry.
Creatively apply this knowledge in professional subjects and in the use of computer technology.
Acquire the basic knowledge of three-dimensional descriptive geometry necessary to solve real life situations in various areas of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Conic sections, focal properties of conic sections, pointwise construction of a conic, osculating circles, construction of a tangent from a given point, diameters and center of a conic, conjugate diameters
Analytic geometry in the plane and in space (problems involving lines and planes, classification of conic sections)
Kinematics, cyclic curves

Central and parallel projection and their properties (point, line, plane, parallel lines, perpendicular lines), collineations between planes, central collineation, axial affinity, ideal points (projective axiom, homogeneous coordinates of proper and ideal points), derivation of parametric equations of kinematic curves in the projective plane
Basics of axonometry, orthographic axonometry – bases of solids and height
orthogonal axonometry – solids and their sections

derivation of the helix parametric equation and its distribution
helical surfaces

Monge projection – solids and their sections
surfaces of revolution, derivation of parametric equations in projective space, construction of surfaces, cross-sections of rotation surfaces

assessment_rules: To obtain course-unit credit, students must draw up 2 semestral works (each at most 5 points) and obtain at least 5 points out of 10 in one written test. The exam has a practical part (up to 80 points for 3 problems) and a theoretical part (up to 20 points). Final classification is based on the sum of points from both exam parts, with 0-49 points being an F, and 90-100 points an A. Attendance at seminars and exercises is compulsory.
